answer.rationale: Price-matching a competitor's deeper discount directly contradicts exp_73 learning: targeted discounting acquired cohorts that failed to retain and convert to revenue on renewal. Memory_73 and exp_73 together show promotional_pricing is unsustainable for SMB at scale. Instead, the durable memory shows three reinforcing levers that drive sustainable activation without retention risk: activation_messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and nudged first meaningful actions; simplify_onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) improved SMB activation and completion rates. Referral_incentive (memory_57) worked in established customers. In a competitive moment with churn pressure, activation_messaging offers the fastest, lowest-risk deployment: it requires no margin sacrifice, replicates the proven week-one engagement lift, and compounds retention by deepening early product value realization—the opposite mechanical outcome of discounting. This buys time before renewal conversations, addresses the root churn signal (low activation, not just price), and aligns with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Deploy activation_messaging at standard experiment scale on churn-risk cohorts; parallel a simplified onboarding refresh to extend the effect. Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to this cohort. Referral_incentive requires an established customer base with existing loyalty—less relevant to active churn defense.
